title: 3. Distribution, Supply Chain & Unit Economics

epigraph.quote: In real estate, accounting profit is an opinion formed by Ind AS 115; cash collected in the RERA escrow account is the only fact that pays down debt.
epigraph.author: Credit Analyst's Rule of Thumb

web_blocks.html: Ajmera's go-to-market engine pairs an entrenched channel-partner (broker) network across MMR and Bengaluru with a strong direct-referral base [1][3]. Five decades of delivering 46,000+ homes built that referral pool [1][3]. Management briefs channel partners weeks ahead of RERA launches through soft-marketing previews [10][14]. That playbook drove 40%+ launch-month sell-through (~₹700 crore) at Manhattan II and 84% absorption in 60 hours at Solis Vikhroli [10][14][18]. Existing homeowners in Bhakti Park and Electronic City also refer buyers for new phases, cutting mass-media ad spend [1]. Brokerage commissions typically run 2% to 4% of booking value, paid against milestone collections.

On the execution side, Ajmera acts as an engineering-led project manager rather than relying solely on turnkey EPC contractors [1][21]. Chairman Rajnikant Ajmera's civil-engineering background anchors that approach [1][21]. In FY26, the company capitalized Mivan aluminium formwork ('slidings') across high-rise sites [8][10]. That investment lifted net Property, Plant & Equipment from ₹35 crore to ₹60+ crore and total Fixed Assets from ₹77 crore to ₹106 crore [8]. Mivan formwork accelerates slab cycles and cuts finishing defects [10]. Steel, cement, and ready-mix concrete still expose margins to commodity inflation. Management also flagged potential Q4 FY27 water shortages in Mumbai as an operational risk [14]. In redevelopment projects, Ajmera absorbs tenant transit rent and corpus obligations until OC handover.

Unit economics follow strict RERA escrow rules: 70% of customer collections must enter project-specific bank accounts [1][14]. Developers can withdraw those funds only against certified percentage-of-completion milestones for land and construction [1][14]. Under Ind AS 115, P&L revenue recognition waits until a project crosses key gates: roughly 25% construction cost incurred, 10%+ collections, and core approvals [11][22]. That rule creates a 4-to-5-quarter lag between pre-sales bookings and reported revenue [11][22]. In FY26, collection efficiency improved to 65% (₹1,103 crore collected on ₹1,701 crore pre-sales, up from 60% in FY25) [10][14]. Weighted average cost of debt also fell from 12.22% in Q3 FY25 to 11.15% in FY26 and 10.75% by Q2 FY27 [10][14][22].

web_blocks.takeaway: Wadala's zero-cost land cushion subsidizes the thinner margins of suburban redevelopment, allowing consolidated OPM to hover around 27–31% across the cycle.

web_blocks.caption: FY26 (Mar 2026) Audited Cash Conversion Waterfall (₹ Crore)
web_blocks.takeaway: Of ₹1,090 Cr recognized revenue in FY26, subtracting ₹792 Cr of consolidated expenses (which bundle Employee Expenses and Other Operating Overhead in Screener's summary format) leaves ₹298 Cr (₹299 Cr reported Operating Profit on Screener due to rounding; 27.4% OPM) and ₹157 Cr Net Profit (14.4%), while working-capital absorption reduced Operating Cash Flow to ₹69 Cr (6.3% of revenue) and Free Cash Flow to ₹40 Cr after ₹29 Cr capex.

web_blocks.title: The P&L vs. Cash-Flow Divergence Explained
paragraphs: In FY26, Ajmera reported ₹1,090 Cr in revenue and ₹157 Cr in PAT [8]. Yet Cash Flow from Operations (CFO) was only ₹69 Cr—a 47% pre-tax CFO/EBITDA ratio, following 21% in FY25 [8]. Construction spending on new launches (Manhattan II, Solis, Vihara, Marina) flows out immediately as work-in-progress inventory. Milestone collections and RERA escrow releases trail that early excavation and podium work.

book_paragraphs: To see why real estate accounting can mislead even seasoned equity analysts, you and I have to trace a single rupee from a homebuyer's cheque all the way to Ajmera's bottom line. When a family books a ₹3 crore apartment at Ajmera Manhattan, they do not pay ₹3 crore on day one. They pay a 10% booking token, followed by construction-linked installments as the tower rises floor by floor. Under RERA rules, 70% of every rupee collected goes straight into a ring-fenced escrow account, where it can only be drawn down against certified construction progress.

Meanwhile, on the income statement, Ind AS 115 imposes a strict gatekeeper. Ajmera cannot book a single rupee of revenue until the project passes roughly 25% of its budgeted construction cost, secures critical approvals, and collects at least 10% from buyers. That creates a natural four-to-five-quarter lag between today's pre-sales headlines and tomorrow's reported revenue. It also explains why Ajmera's collection efficiency—₹1,103 crore collected in FY26 against ₹1,701 crore of pre-sales, or 65%—is a far cleaner pulse check than quarterly P&L swings.

On the cost side, Ajmera has invested in owning its Mivan aluminium formwork rather than renting it piecemeal, lifting its property, plant, and equipment base from ₹35 crore to over ₹60 crore in FY26. Mivan formwork lets crews pour walls and slabs in a single monolithic cycle, shaving months off high-rise timelines. Yet look closely at the FY26 cash-conversion waterfall: out of ₹1,090 crore in revenue, subtracting ₹792 crore of consolidated expenses (which bundle employee expenses and operating overhead in Screener's summary format) leaves ₹298 crore (₹299 crore rounded operating profit on Screener) and ₹157 crore of net profit, while only ₹69 crore emerged as operating cash flow, leaving ₹40 crore of free cash flow after ₹29 crore of capital expenditure. Until ongoing towers finish their heavy podium and superstructure spend and enter the high-collection finishing stage, working capital will continue to absorb a large share of accounting profits.

You also need to appreciate how differently unit economics behave between Wadala and suburban redevelopment. In Wadala, where Ajmera owns the land at near-zero historical cost, selling at ₹35,000 per square foot against ₹6,000 per square foot of construction and podium costs leaves enormous room for profit. In a suburban society redevelopment like Bhandup, Ajmera must first build free apartments for existing residents and pay monthly transit rent while they wait—which compresses project EBITDA margins into the mid-twenties even though upfront land capital is minimal.

book_callouts.title: Watch the Cost of Debt and Working Capital
book_callouts.text: Even after cutting its weighted average cost of debt from 12.20% to 10.75% by Q2 FY27, Ajmera paid ₹73 crore in FY26 interest—nearly 24% of its operating profit. Sustaining 65%+ collection efficiency is essential to keep debt-service coverage comfortable.

book_callouts.title: Why Mivan Capex Signals Execution Confidence
book_callouts.text: Capitalizing Mivan formwork onto the balance sheet only makes financial sense when a developer has a multi-year pipeline of standardized high-rise towers—exactly what Ajmera has in Wadala and central Mumbai.

book_subsections.title: How Channel Partners Drive Launch Velocity
paragraphs: Unlike consumer brands that spend heavily on television advertising, mid-tier Mumbai developers live and die by channel-partner activation. Ajmera's sales teams brief hundreds of local brokers ahead of RERA registration, creating pent-up booking queues on launch weekend. That distribution muscle works remarkably well for mass-affluent products like Solis in Vikhroli and Manhattan II in Wadala, though brokerage commissions (typically 2% to 4% of booking value) are a recurring selling expense.

Equally important is repeat and referral demand from Ajmera's existing 46,000-home customer base. In townships like Bhakti Park and Electronic City, satisfied residents upgrading to larger 3 or 4 BHK units provide a zero-marketing-cost buyer pool that stabilizes sustenance sales long after launch weekend fades.
